school.tagged_body:
Last Saturday, I {{g:went to|go의 과거형 went: ~에 갔다}} a malatang restaurant with my friend Mina. It was my first time there. Mina helped me choose my food.

I put {{v:noodles}}, {{v:cabbage}}, {{v:mushrooms}}, and {{v:tofu}} into my {{v:bowl}}. They looked {{v:delicious}}. I wanted more noodles, but my bowl was already {{v:full}}. Mina laughed.

{{g:We both chose|both: 둘 다; chose는 choose의 과거형}} the {{v:mild}} soup. It was still a little {{v:spicy}} for me. I drank some water and ate {{v:slowly}}.

Next time, {{g:I will choose|will + 동사원형: 앞으로 ~할 것이다}} less spicy soup. Mina asked, "And fewer noodles?" I looked at my big bowl and laughed. {{t:I enjoyed the food and my time with Mina.}}

grammar: both: 둘 다; chose는 choose의 과거형

questions.q: 글쓴이는 언제 마라탕 식당에 갔나요?
questions.explanation: 근거: "Last Saturday" Last Saturday가 방문 시점이다.

questions.q: 함께 식당에 간 사람은 누구인가요?
questions.explanation: 근거: "with my friend Mina" 미나는 글쓴이의 친구이다.

questions.q: 이 식당 방문은 글쓴이에게 몇 번째였나요?
questions.explanation: 근거: "It was my first time there." first time은 첫 방문이라는 뜻이다.

questions.q: 그릇에 넣은 재료끼리 바르게 묶인 것은?
questions.explanation: 근거: "I put noodles, cabbage, mushrooms, and tofu into my bowl." 열거된 네 재료와 모두 일치하는 보기이다.

questions.q: 면을 더 넣고 싶었을 때 그릇은 어떤 상태였나요?
questions.explanation: 근거: "my bowl was already full" already full은 이미 가득 차 있다는 뜻이다.

questions.q: 두 사람이 고른 국물은 무엇인가요?
questions.explanation: 근거: "We both chose the mild soup." both는 둘 다, mild는 순한 맛을 뜻한다.

questions.q: 국물이 조금 맵게 느껴진 뒤 글쓴이가 한 일은?
questions.explanation: 근거: "I drank some water and ate slowly." drank water와 ate slowly 두 행동을 확인한다.

questions.q: 다음번 국물 선택 계획은 무엇인가요?
questions.explanation: 근거: "Next time, I will choose less spicy soup." less spicy는 덜 매운이라는 뜻이다.

questions.q: 미나가 fewer noodles라고 물은 이유와 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: 미나가 면을 전혀 먹지 못하기 때문에
이번에 면을 더 넣으려다 그릇이 가득 찼기 때문에
questions.answer: 이번에 면을 더 넣으려다 그릇이 가득 찼기 때문에
questions.explanation: 근거: "I wanted more noodles, but my bowl was already full." 앞의 면 선택과 연결되는 짧은 농담이다. 없는 알레르기·재고·이사는 추측하지 않는다.

questions.q: 글 마지막에서 즐거웠다고 한 것은?
questions.explanation: 근거: "I enjoyed the food and my time with Mina." 음식과 친구와 함께한 시간 모두를 즐겼다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (도와주었다)
Mina ___ me choose my food.
questions.explanation: "Mina helped me choose my food." 문맥상 '도와주었다'에 해당하는 단어는 helped이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (맛있는)
They looked ___.
questions.explanation: "They looked delicious." 문맥상 '맛있는'에 해당하는 단어는 delicious이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (물)
I drank some ___ and ate slowly.
questions.explanation: "I drank some water and ate slowly." 문맥상 '물'에 해당하는 단어는 water이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (둘 다)
We ___ chose the mild soup.
questions.explanation: "We both chose the mild soup." 문맥상 '둘 다'에 해당하는 단어는 both이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (웃었다)
I looked at my big bowl and ___.
questions.explanation: "I looked at my big bowl and laughed." 문맥상 '웃었다'에 해당하는 단어는 laughed이다.

questions.q: 글쓴이는 그 식당에 여러 번 가 본 상태였다.
questions.explanation: 근거: "It was my first time there." 첫 방문이므로 여러 번 가 본 상태가 아니다.

questions.q: 미나는 글쓴이가 음식을 고르는 것을 도왔다.
questions.explanation: 근거: "Mina helped me choose my food." 도움을 주었다고 직접 제시된다.

questions.q: 순한 국물을 골랐지만 글쓴이에게는 조금 매웠다.
questions.explanation: 근거: "It was still a little spicy for me." 순한 국물을 고른 앞 문장과 이어 읽는다.

questions.q: 다음 새 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 것은? Yesterday, Jisu ___ a cake.
questions.explanation: 근거: "I drank some water" Yesterday는 과거 시점이므로 make의 과거형 made를 쓴다. 본문 drank도 drink의 과거형이다.

questions.q: 영어 단어와 이 지문에서의 우리말 뜻을 짝지으세요.
questions.explanation: 식재료 이름과 문맥에서의 맛 표현을 연결한다.

essays.q:
[조건 영작] 나는 어제 미나와 공원에 갔다.
〈조건〉 I로 시작 / go를 과거형으로 바꾸기 / with Mina, to the park, yesterday를 각각 한 번 사용
essays.sampleAnswer: I went to the park with Mina yesterday.
essays.rubric: ① 공원·미나·어제의 의미 ② go→went ③ 제시어 각1회. I went with Mina to the park yesterday. 등 자연스러운 어순 인정.

essays.q:
[문장 전환] 다음 문장을 yesterday를 사용한 과거 문장으로 바꾸세요.
I drink some milk.
〈조건〉 I로 시작 / drink의 과거형 사용
essays.sampleAnswer: I drank some milk yesterday.
essays.rubric: ① drank ② some milk의 의미 보존 ③ yesterday를 한 번 포함. I로 시작하는 자연스러운 어순 인정.

essays.q:
[오류 선택·수정] 어제 한 일을 나타낼 때 틀린 문장 한 개를 골라 기호를 쓰고 바르게 고치세요.
A. I played soccer yesterday.
B. I go to the park yesterday.
C. I ate lunch yesterday.
〈조건〉 뜻은 유지 / 틀린 동사를 과거형으로 수정
essays.sampleAnswer: B. I went to the park yesterday.
essays.rubric: ① B선택 ② go→went ③ 나머지 의미 보존. 기호와 수정 문장을 구분해 부분 평가한다.

essays.q:
[조건 영작] 내 그릇은 가득 차 있다.
〈조건〉 My bowl로 시작 / is, full을 각각 한 번 사용
essays.sampleAnswer: My bowl is full.
essays.rubric: ① My bowl ② is ③ full과 완전한 문장. 현재 상태이므로 was는 조건 미충족.

essays.q:
[문장 전환] 빈칸이 없는 부정문으로 바꾸세요.
I like spicy soup.
〈조건〉 I로 시작 / do not 사용 / 나머지 뜻은 유지
essays.sampleAnswer: I do not like spicy soup.
essays.rubric: ① do not ② like 원형 ③ spicy soup 보존. 조건이 do not이므로 축약형은 이 문제에서 인정하지 않음.

academy.tagged_body:
Last Saturday, I went to a malatang restaurant with my friend Mina. It was my first time there, so I did not know {{g:what to choose|의문사 + to부정사: 무엇을 고를지}}.

"First, pick the things you want to eat," Mina said.

I put {{v:noodles}}, {{v:cabbage}}, {{v:mushrooms}}, and {{v:tofu}} into my {{v:bowl}}. Everything looked {{v:delicious}}. Then I {{v:reached for}} more noodles.

"Your bowl is already {{v:full}}!" Mina said with a laugh.

We both chose the {{v:mild}} soup. {{g:However|앞 내용과 대조되는 상황 연결}}, when I took my first {{v:bite}}, it was still a little {{v:spicy}} for me. I drank some water and {{g:ate more|more + 부사: 더 천천히 먹었다}} {{v:slowly}}.

"Next time, I'll choose less spicy soup," I said.

Mina smiled. "And fewer noodles?"

I looked at my big bowl and laughed. The food was good, but {{t:eating with Mina was the best part.}}

questions.q: Why did the writer not know what to choose?
choices: The writer had lost the bowl.
questions.explanation: 근거: "It was my first time there, so I did not know what to choose." so 앞에 처음 방문했다는 직접적인 이유가 나온다.

questions.q: What did Mina tell the writer to do first?
choices: Pick the things the writer wanted to eat.
Drink a large glass of cold water.
Find a table far away from her.
Ask for the spiciest soup on the menu.
Give the full bowl to another friend.
questions.answer: Pick the things the writer wanted to eat.
questions.explanation: 근거: "First, pick the things you want to eat" 먼저 원하는 재료를 고르라는 말이다.

questions.q: Which ingredient was NOT listed in the writer's bowl?
questions.explanation: 근거: "I put noodles, cabbage, mushrooms, and tofu into my bowl." 네 재료 중 cheese는 없다.

questions.q: What did the writer reach for after filling the bowl?
questions.explanation: 근거: "Then I reached for more noodles." 직접 언급된 것은 면이다.

questions.q: How did Mina point out that the bowl was full?
choices: She wrote it on the menu.
She said it with a laugh.
questions.answer: She said it with a laugh.
questions.explanation: 근거: "Mina said with a laugh" 웃으며 말했지 화를 내거나 자리를 떠난 것이 아니다.

questions.q: What did BOTH friends choose?
questions.explanation: 근거: "We both chose the mild soup." both와 mild soup를 확인한다.

questions.q: How did the first bite taste to the writer?
questions.explanation: 근거: "it was still a little spicy for me" 순한 맛이었지만 글쓴이에게는 조금 매웠다.

questions.q: Which action did the writer take after that bite?
choices: Drinking water and eating more slowly.
Putting more noodles into the bowl.
Asking Mina to stop eating her food.
questions.answer: Drinking water and eating more slowly.
questions.explanation: 근거: "I drank some water and ate more slowly." 물을 마시고 더 천천히 먹었다.

questions.q: What does "fewer" in Mina's question refer to?
choices: A lower price for the soup.
A shorter visit with the friend.
questions.explanation: 근거: "And fewer noodles?" noodles의 양을 줄인다는 농담이다. 가격·통학 시간 등의 의미가 아니다.

questions.q: What was the best part of the visit for the writer?
questions.explanation: 근거: "eating with Mina was the best part" 친구와 함께 먹는 시간이 가장 좋았다고 명시한다.

questions.explanation: "Everything looked delicious." 문맥상 '맛있는'에 해당하는 단어는 delicious이다.

questions.q:

Then I reached for more ___.
questions.explanation: "Then I reached for more noodles." 문맥상 '면'에 해당하는 단어는 noodles이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (순한)
We both chose the ___ soup.
questions.explanation: "We both chose the mild soup." 문맥상 '순한'에 해당하는 단어는 mild이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (천천히)
I drank some water and ate more ___.
questions.explanation: "I drank some water and ate more slowly." 문맥상 '천천히'에 해당하는 단어는 slowly이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (미소 지었다)
Mina ___.
questions.explanation: "Mina smiled." 문맥상 '미소 지었다'에 해당하는 단어는 smiled이다.

questions.q: 글쓴이는 다음번에 더 매운 국물을 고르겠다고 했다.
questions.explanation: 근거: "I'll choose less spicy soup" less는 덜이라는 뜻이므로 더 매운 것을 고른다는 말이 아니다.

questions.q: 미나는 그릇이 가득 찼다는 말을 웃으며 했다.
questions.explanation: 근거: "Mina said with a laugh" with a laugh라는 표현이 있다.

questions.q: 글쓴이는 음식이 좋았지만 미나와 먹는 시간이 가장 좋았다고 했다.
questions.explanation: 근거: "The food was good, but eating with Mina was the best part." but 뒤에 가장 좋았던 점이 제시된다.

questions.q: Choose the correct form for this NEW sentence: Yesterday, Hana ___ her room.
questions.explanation: 새 문장의 Yesterday는 과거 시점이다. clean의 과거형 cleaned가 맞다. cleans는 현재형이고 나머지는 과거 문장의 본동사로 쓸 수 없다. 본문 답안 표현을 그대로 복사하는 문제와 구별한다.

questions.q: 영어 단어와 이 지문에서의 우리말 뜻을 짝지으세요.
questions.explanation: 식재료 이름과 문맥에서의 맛 표현을 연결한다.

essays.q:
[조건 영작] 나는 지난 일요일에 친구와 점심을 먹었다.
〈조건〉 I로 시작 / eat을 과거형으로 변경 / lunch, with my friend, last Sunday 각각 한 번 사용
essays.sampleAnswer: I ate lunch with my friend last Sunday.
essays.rubric: ① 주어진 우리말 ② ate ③ 제시어 각1회. Last Sunday의 문두 이동은 I시작 조건 때문에 불가.

essays.q:
[문장 전환] tomorrow를 사용한 미래 문장으로 바꾸세요.
I choose a small bowl.
〈조건〉 I로 시작 / will 사용 / small bowl의 의미 유지
essays.sampleAnswer: I will choose a small bowl tomorrow.
essays.rubric: ① will choose ② a small bowl ③ tomorrow. 의미가 같은 자연스러운 어순 인정.

essays.q:
[오류 선택·수정] 어법상 틀린 문장 한 개의 기호를 쓰고 고치세요.
A. Mina drank some water.
B. We chose mild soup.
C. I will ate slowly.
〈조건〉 미래의 뜻 유지 / 틀린 부분만 수정
essays.sampleAnswer: C. I will eat slowly.
essays.rubric: ① C선택 ② will 뒤 eat원형 ③ 미래 의미 보존. 기호만 맞힌 것과 수정까지 한 것을 구분 평가.

essays.q:
[조건 영작] 그 국물은 나에게 조금 맵다.
〈조건〉 The soup로 시작 / is, a little, spicy, for me 각각 한 번 사용
essays.sampleAnswer: The soup is a little spicy for me.
essays.rubric: ① 국물과 개인 느낌 ② is a little spicy ③ for me와 제시어 각1회.

essays.q:
[문장 전환] 다음 두 문장을 but으로 연결하세요.
The bowl was full. I wanted more noodles.
〈조건〉 The bowl로 시작 / 두 내용 모두 유지
essays.sampleAnswer: The bowl was full, but I wanted more noodles.
essays.rubric: ① 두 내용 보존 ② but으로 대조 ③ 하나의 완전한 문장. 쉼표 유무는 별도 감점하지 않음.

advanced.tagged_body:
Last Saturday, I went to a malatang restaurant with my friend Mina. It was my first time there, so I needed help choosing my food. "Pick the things you want to eat," Mina explained.

I put {{v:noodles}}, {{v:cabbage}}, {{v:mushrooms}}, and {{v:tofu}} into my {{v:bowl}}. Everything looked so {{v:delicious}} {{g:that I reached for|so + 형용사 + that절: 너무 맛있어 보여서 ~하다}} more noodles. "Your bowl is already {{v:full}}!" Mina said with a laugh. I looked down and {{v:noticed}} {{g:how much food I had chosen|얼마나 많은 음식을 골랐는지 나타내는 절}}.

We both chose the {{v:mild}} soup. However, the first bite was still a little {{v:spicy}} for me. The word "mild" did not mean the soup {{g:would taste the same|taste + 형용사: 같은 맛으로 느껴지다}} to both of us. I drank some water and ate more {{v:slowly}}.

"Next time, I'll choose less spicy soup," I said. "And fewer noodles?" Mina asked with a smile. I looked at my big bowl and laughed. Her joke {{v:reminded}} me of my choices. The food was good, but {{v:sharing}} this new {{v:experience}} with Mina {{t:was the best part.}}

grammar: so + 형용사 + that절: 너무 맛있어 보여서 ~하다
얼마나 많은 음식을 골랐는지 나타내는 절

questions.q: Which detail explains why Mina's help was useful at the start?
choices: The writer was an expert at making malatang.
Mina had already eaten every ingredient.
The writer had not visited the restaurant before.
The restaurant did not allow anyone to choose food.
The writer had brought a bowl from home.
questions.answer: The writer had not visited the restaurant before.
questions.explanation: 근거: "It was my first time there, so I needed help choosing my food." 첫 방문이라 재료 고르는 도움이 필요했다.

questions.q: What attracted the writer to choosing more noodles?
choices: The bowl was too small to hold any food.
Mina had asked the writer to hurry home.
The writer had decided not to eat any vegetables.
The soup was promised to be completely cold.
questions.explanation: 근거: "Everything looked so delicious that I reached for more noodles." 맛있어 보여 면에 손이 갔다는 인과관계다.

questions.q: What did the writer notice after Mina's first comment?
choices: How little time remained before school.
How expensive every dish on the menu was.
How empty Mina's bowl had become.
How far the restaurant was from home.
How much food was already chosen.
questions.answer: How much food was already chosen.
questions.explanation: 근거: "I looked down and noticed how much food I had chosen." 음식의 양을 알아차렸다. 가격·거리·시간은 없다.

questions.q: Which choice was shared by the two friends?
choices: Drinking the same amount of water.
questions.explanation: 근거: "We both chose the mild soup." 순한 국물 선택은 공통이고 물의 양 등은 제시되지 않았다.

questions.q: Why is "However" used before the description of the first bite?
choices: The writer found out that Mina had gone home.
The first bite was much sweeter than a dessert.
The soup contained none of the chosen food.
The mild soup still felt spicy to the writer.
The restaurant suddenly changed into a shop.
questions.answer: The mild soup still felt spicy to the writer.
questions.explanation: 근거: "However, the first bite was still a little spicy for me." 순한 맛 선택과 실제로 맵게 느낀 경험을 대조한다.

questions.q: What can we conclude about Mina's own reaction to the soup?
choices: She certainly could not eat even one bite.
The passage does not tell us exactly how spicy it felt to her.
She definitely thought it was not spicy at all.
She asked the writer to choose the hottest soup.
She needed more water than the writer did.
questions.answer: The passage does not tell us exactly how spicy it felt to her.
questions.explanation: 근거: "The word "mild" did not mean the soup would taste the same to both of us." 사람에 따라 느낌이 같다고 보장되지 않는다. 미나의 실제 반응을 글이 구체적으로 말하지 않으므로 단정할 수 없다.

questions.q: What is Mina's short question about fewer noodles connected to?
choices: A rule that the restaurant never serves noodles.
The writer's promise to buy a smaller restaurant.
A lesson about how to cook mushrooms at home.
Mina's plan to avoid eating with friends again.
The writer's earlier attempt to add noodles to a full bowl.
questions.answer: The writer's earlier attempt to add noodles to a full bowl.
questions.explanation: 근거: "Your bowl is already full!" 앞의 양 선택을 가볍게 다시 떠올리게 하는 농담이다.

questions.q: Which response shows that the writer accepted Mina's joke in a friendly way?
choices: Looking at the bowl and laughing.
Refusing to speak to Mina again.
Throwing the noodles on the floor.
Asking Mina to pay for every meal.
questions.answer: Looking at the bowl and laughing.
questions.explanation: 근거: "I looked at my big bowl and laughed." 그릇을 보고 함께 웃는 행동이 친근한 반응을 보여 준다.

questions.q: Which lesson best fits the writer's experience with food choices?
choices: Every person always enjoys exactly the same soup.
Choosing the most food always makes a visit better.
A familiar menu word removes the need to notice our own reactions.
Something can look tempting before we consider the amount or taste.
Friends should make every food choice without asking us.
questions.answer: Something can look tempting before we consider the amount or taste.
questions.explanation: 근거: "Everything looked so delicious that I reached for more noodles." 맛있어 보이는 재료에 이끌렸지만 양과 실제 매운 정도는 먹을 사람에게 맞춰 볼 필요가 있음을 이야기에서 생각할 수 있다.

questions.q: Which title best covers both the food and the friendship in the passage?
choices: The Recipe That Made Mina Famous
Why the Writer Stopped Seeing Mina
A New Meal and a Shared Laugh
A Restaurant Without Any Food Choices
How to Win a Fast-Eating Contest
questions.answer: A New Meal and a Shared Laugh
questions.explanation: 근거: "sharing this new experience with Mina was the best part" 새 음식 경험과 친구와 나눈 즐거움을 모두 포함한다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (설명했다)
Mina ___.
questions.explanation: "Mina explained." 문맥상 '설명했다'에 해당하는 단어는 explained이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (둘 다)
We ___ chose the mild soup.
questions.explanation: "We both chose the mild soup." 문맥상 '둘 다'에 해당하는 단어는 both이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (천천히)
I drank some water and ate more ___.
questions.explanation: "I drank some water and ate more slowly." 문맥상 '천천히'에 해당하는 단어는 slowly이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (농담)
Her ___ reminded me of my choices.
questions.explanation: "Her joke reminded me of my choices." 문맥상 '농담'에 해당하는 단어는 joke이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (웃었다)
I looked at my big bowl and ___.
questions.explanation: "I looked at my big bowl and laughed." 문맥상 '웃었다'에 해당하는 단어는 laughed이다.

questions.q: 본문은 순한 맛을 고르면 누구에게나 전혀 맵지 않다고 보장한다.
questions.explanation: 근거: "The word "mild" did not mean the soup would taste the same to both of us." 사람마다 느끼는 정도가 같다고 보장하지 않는다.

questions.q: 글쓴이는 다음번 국물을 덜 맵게 고르려 한다.
questions.explanation: 근거: "Next time, I'll choose less spicy soup" 덜 매운 국물을 고르겠다는 계획이다.

questions.q: 미나의 농담을 들은 뒤 글쓴이는 자신의 음식 선택을 떠올렸다.
questions.explanation: 근거: "Her joke reminded me of my choices." 농담이 자신의 선택을 생각나게 했다.

questions.q: 다음 새 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 것은? The red bag is ___ than the blue bag. (빨간 가방이 더 무겁다.)
questions.explanation: than과 두 가방의 비교 의미에 맞는 heavy의 비교급은 heavier이다. y를 i로 바꾸고 -er을 붙인다. heaviest는 최상급이고 more heavy는 이 문항의 표준 비교급 형태가 아니다.

questions.q: 영어 단어와 이 지문에서의 우리말 뜻을 짝지으세요.
questions.explanation: 식재료 이름과 문맥에서의 맛 표현을 연결한다.

essays.q:
[조건 영작] 나는 배가 고파서 빵을 더 집었다.
〈조건〉 I로 시작 / because 사용 / hungry, reached for, more bread 각각 한 번 사용 / 과거 시제
essays.sampleAnswer: I reached for more bread because I was hungry.
essays.rubric: ① 배고픔과 더 집은 행동의 인과 ② because 뒤 완전한 절 ③ 과거 시제와 제시어 각1회. I was hungry because I reached...처럼 원인과 결과가 뒤집힌 답은 내용 점수 불인정.

essays.q:
[문장 전환] slowly의 비교 표현을 사용해 한 문장으로 쓰세요.
Mina ate slowly. I ate even more slowly.
〈조건〉 I로 시작 / than Mina 사용 / 누가 더 천천히 먹었는지 유지
essays.sampleAnswer: I ate more slowly than Mina.
essays.rubric: ① I ate ② more slowly ③ than Mina. faster로 바꾸면 제시 조건 불충족. 실제 이야기 속 사실이 아니라 제공한 새 두 문장의 전환이다.

essays.q:
[오류 선택·수정] 어법상 틀린 문장 두 개의 기호를 쓰고 각각 고치세요.
A. We both chose mild soup.
B. She drink water yesterday.
C. I will chose a smaller bowl.
D. The noodles looked delicious.
〈조건〉 B는 과거, C는 미래 의미 유지 / 잘못된 동사 형태만 수정
essays.sampleAnswer:
B. She drank water yesterday.
C. I will choose a smaller bowl.
essays.rubric: ① B와 C선택 ② B의drank ③ C의will choose. 각 기호와 수정 내용을 구분하여 부분 평가. A,D를 오류로 고치면 해당 부분은 불인정.

essays.q:
[조건 영작] 같은 국물도 모든 사람에게 똑같은 맛으로 느껴지지는 않는다.
〈조건〉 The same soup로 시작 / does not, taste, the same, to everyone 각각 한 번 사용
essays.sampleAnswer: The same soup does not taste the same to everyone.
essays.rubric: ① 사람별 느낌이 같다는 보장을 부정 ② does not taste ③ 제시어 각1회. 모두가 반드시 다르게 느낀다고 과장하면 의미 불일치.

essays.q:
[문장 전환] 다음 두 문장을 so로 연결하세요.
It was my first visit. I needed help choosing food.
〈조건〉 It로 시작 / 원인과 결과 유지
essays.sampleAnswer: It was my first visit, so I needed help choosing food.
essays.rubric: ① 첫방문 원인 ② 선택도움 필요 결과 ③ so로 연결한 한 문장. 두 절 순서를 뒤집으면 It시작 조건과 인과 관계 확인.

prestudy.tagged_body:
Last Saturday, I went to a malatang restaurant with my friend Mina. It was my first visit, so I did not know how to choose my food. Mina {{g:told me to pick|tell + 목적어 + to부정사: ~에게 고르라고 말하다}} the things I wanted to eat.

I put {{v:noodles}}, {{v:cabbage}}, {{v:mushrooms}}, and {{v:tofu}} into my {{v:bowl}}. Everything looked {{v:delicious}}, and I reached for more noodles. "Your bowl is already {{v:full}}!" Mina said with a laugh. I was choosing with my eyes {{v:instead of}} thinking about {{g:how much I could eat|의문사절: 내가 얼마나 먹을 수 있는지}}.

We both chose the {{v:mild}} soup. {{g:Although|although + 문장: 비록 ~이지만}} it was called "mild," the first bite was still a little {{v:spicy}} for me. The same word on a menu does not tell us {{v:exactly}} how everyone will feel. I drank some water and ate more {{v:slowly}}.

Next time, I will choose less spicy soup and think more {{v:carefully}} about the {{v:amount}} of food. "And fewer noodles?" Mina asked with a smile. I looked at my big bowl and laughed. She did not need to give me a long lesson. Her short question helped me {{v:notice}} something for myself. The food was good, but {{t:enjoying a new experience with a friend mattered most.}}

grammar: 의문사절: 내가 얼마나 먹을 수 있는지

questions.q: What did Mina first help the writer understand?
choices: How to open a restaurant alone.
How to make every soup taste sweet.
How to choose food for the bowl.
How to leave without ordering anything.
How to cook noodles for a large party.
questions.answer: How to choose food for the bowl.
questions.explanation: 근거: "Mina told me to pick the things I wanted to eat." 원하는 재료를 고르라는 도움이다.

questions.q: Which ingredients appear in the writer's bowl?
questions.explanation: 근거: "I put noodles, cabbage, mushrooms, and tofu into my bowl." 본문의 네 재료를 직접 확인하는 기본 문항이다.

questions.q: What happened when the writer wanted more noodles?
choices: Mina asked for another bowl of the hottest soup.
The writer found that the restaurant had no noodles.
The writer decided to leave before eating the meal.
Mina told the writer to throw away all the vegetables.
Mina pointed out that the bowl was already full.
questions.answer: Mina pointed out that the bowl was already full.
questions.explanation: 근거: "Your bowl is already full!" 미나는 이미 가득 찬 그릇을 알려 주었다.

questions.q: What does "choosing with my eyes" mean in this story?
choices: Being unable to see any food in the restaurant.
Being attracted by how delicious the food looked.
Closing the eyes to make a random choice.
Reading every price before picking any food.
Looking for Mina because she had gone outside.
questions.answer: Being attracted by how delicious the food looked.
questions.explanation: 근거: "Everything looked delicious, and I reached for more noodles." 맛있어 보이는 것에 이끌려 양을 생각하지 않고 더 고르려 했다는 비유적 표현이다.

questions.q: How did the writer react to the first bite?
choices: By immediately asking for hotter soup.
By refusing to look at the bowl again.
By giving the entire meal to another customer.
By drinking water and eating more slowly.
By leaving Mina to finish the food alone.
questions.answer: By drinking water and eating more slowly.
questions.explanation: 근거: "I drank some water and ate more slowly." 본문에서 직접 확인할 수 있는 행동이다.

questions.q: What does the writer plan to consider more carefully next time?
choices: The restaurant's opening date and the price of its tables.
The amount of food as well as how spicy the soup is.
The number of friends at school and their favorite games.
The recipe for every mushroom and the color of the menu.
The restaurant's address and the time of the next school test.
questions.answer: The amount of food as well as how spicy the soup is.
questions.explanation: 근거: "I will choose less spicy soup and think more carefully about the amount of food." 매운 정도와 양을 함께 고려한다.

questions.q: What does "Her short question" refer to?
choices: Mina asking whether the writer had a new school.
The writer asking for the spiciest soup.
The writer asking Mina to pay for the meal.
Mina asking how to cook every vegetable.
questions.explanation: 근거: "And fewer noodles?" 직전의 짧은 질문을 가리킨다.

questions.q: Why does the story say a menu word cannot tell us exactly how everyone will feel?
choices: A description does not guarantee that different people will have the same experience.
A menu never contains any useful information about food.
Every friend must choose a different restaurant to enjoy a meal.
The writer can know Mina's feelings without asking her anything.
All soups with different names taste exactly the same to everyone.
questions.answer: A description does not guarantee that different people will have the same experience.
questions.explanation: 근거: "The same word on a menu does not tell us exactly how everyone will feel." 같은 표기와 개인 경험을 구별하는 도전 문항이다. 메뉴 정보가 전혀 쓸모없다는 과장으로 확대하지 않는다.

questions.q: Which new situation is most similar to the lesson about choosing food?
choices: A child takes every cake because a bigger plate must always be better.
A child assumes that a sweet label means every friend will like the same cake.
A child refuses to listen when a friend gently points out a full plate.
A child sees many nice cakes but considers how much they can eat before taking more.
A child decides that eating with a friend can never be enjoyable.
questions.answer: A child sees many nice cakes but considers how much they can eat before taking more.
questions.explanation: 근거: "thinking about how much I could eat" 새 상황에 양을 생각하는 배움을 적용한다. 무조건 많이 고르거나 남의 느낌을 단정하는 것은 이야기와 다르다.

questions.q: How does Mina's question help the writer without a long lesson?
choices: It proves that the writer will never enjoy noodles again.
It explains every step for cooking malatang at home.
It connects the earlier full bowl with a possible better choice next time.
It forces the writer to choose exactly the same amount as Mina.
It shows that friendship depends on always ordering the same food.
questions.answer: It connects the earlier full bowl with a possible better choice next time.
questions.explanation: 근거: "Her short question helped me notice something for myself." 앞 장면과 다음 선택을 학생 스스로 연결하게 하는 질문이다. 친구의 양을 강요하거나 면을 금지하는 내용은 없다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (방문)
It was my first ___, so I did not know how to choose my food.
questions.explanation: "It was my first visit, so I did not know how to choose my food." 문맥상 '방문'에 해당하는 단어는 visit이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (순한)
We both chose the ___ soup.
questions.explanation: "We both chose the mild soup." 문맥상 '순한'에 해당하는 단어는 mild이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (물)
I drank some ___ and ate more slowly.
questions.explanation: "I drank some water and ate more slowly." 문맥상 '물'에 해당하는 단어는 water이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (알아차리다)
Her short question helped me ___ something for myself.
questions.explanation: "Her short question helped me notice something for myself." 문맥상 '알아차리다'에 해당하는 단어는 notice이다.

questions.q:
본문과 같은 단어로 빈칸을 채우세요. (교훈이나 가르침)
She did not need to give me a long ___.
questions.explanation: "She did not need to give me a long lesson." 문맥상 '교훈이나 가르침'에 해당하는 단어는 lesson이다.

questions.q: 본문은 식당의 순한 국물이 잘못 만들어졌다고 확정한다.
questions.explanation: 근거: "the first bite was still a little spicy for me" 글쓴이에게 조금 매웠다고 할 뿐 조리 오류를 확인한 것이 아니다.

questions.q: 글쓴이는 다음번 음식의 양도 더 신중하게 생각하려 한다.
questions.explanation: 근거: "think more carefully about the amount of food" 양을 고려하겠다고 직접 말한다.

questions.q: 글의 마지막에서는 친구와 함께한 경험의 즐거움이 강조된다.
questions.explanation: 근거: "enjoying a new experience with a friend mattered most" 친구와 새로운 경험을 즐긴 것이 가장 중요했다고 마무리한다.

questions.q: 다음 새 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 것은? Tomorrow, Mina will ___ her bike.
questions.explanation: will 뒤에는 동사원형 ride를 쓴다. rides·rode·riding·to ride는 이 자리에 맞지 않는다. 본문과 다른 동사로 미래 표현을 적용한다.

questions.q: 영어 단어와 이 지문에서의 우리말 뜻을 짝지으세요.
questions.explanation: 식재료 이름과 문맥에서의 맛 표현을 연결한다.

essays.q:
[조건 영작] 나는 내일 음식의 양을 더 신중하게 생각할 것이다.
〈조건〉 I로 시작 / will, think, more carefully, about the amount of food, tomorrow 각각 한 번 사용
essays.sampleAnswer: I will think more carefully about the amount of food tomorrow.
essays.rubric: ① 미래 계획 의미 ② will think ③ 제시어 각1회. 자연스러운 부사 위치 대체 허용.

essays.q:
[문장 전환] 다음 직접 인용을 told를 사용한 문장으로 바꾸세요.
Mina said to me, "Choose a small bowl."
〈조건〉 Mina로 시작 / told me to 사용 / 원래 부탁의 내용 유지
essays.sampleAnswer: Mina told me to choose a small bowl.
essays.rubric: ① 말하는 사람과 듣는 사람 보존 ② told me to choose ③ a small bowl 보존. 본문 내용을 그대로 베끼지 않는 새 문장 전환이다.

essays.q:
[오류 선택·수정] 어법상 틀린 문장 두 개를 골라 기호와 수정 문장을 쓰세요.
A. I will think carefully next time.
B. Mina told me choose a bowl.
C. I ate more slowly than before.
D. She did not drank any water.
〈조건〉 원래 의미 유지 / 잘못된 부분만 수정
essays.sampleAnswer:
B. Mina told me to choose a bowl.
D. She did not drink any water.
essays.rubric: ① B,D선택 ② told me to choose ③ did not drink. 기호·각목표구조를 따로 부분 평가하며 올바른 A,C를 잘못 수정하지 않는다.

essays.q:
[조건 영작] 그 국물은 순했지만 나에게는 여전히 매웠다.
〈조건〉 Although로 시작 / the soup, mild, still, spicy, for me 사용 / 과거 시제 / but 사용 금지
essays.sampleAnswer: Although the soup was mild, it was still spicy for me.
essays.rubric: ① 순한 표기와 개인 느낌 대조 ② Although절과 완전한 주절 ③ 과거형·필수어·but금지. 주절에서 the soup를 다시 쓰는 답도 조건에 맞으면 인정.

essays.q:
